text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: P1 latency spike detected in inference-runner (continuous-batching path). p95 ~ 800ms (ok), p99 ~ 2.1s (breach), streaming stalls observed. Please triage.

Alice Chen: I'm on it. Which customer routes? any change around rollout? :eyes:

infra-bot: Alerts: cluster-prod-us-west-2 - runner-replicas: increased CPU, GPU memory stable. Queue depth for cont-batch queue spiked to 3.2k.

Maya Ortiz: Seeing a big tail in the cont-batching histogram on the dashboard: median fine, but 99.9th -> 3s. The streaming path is timing out at 10s in some sessions.

Raj Patel: Noted mixed sequence lengths. Heatmap shows a bump in >1024 token requests from a single customer namespace around 1851233500-1851234200. Could be a few long sequences stalling batch fill.

Alice Chen: Reproduced locally with a mixed seqlen mix. Continuous batching is grouping long requests with short ones, causing serialization/paging on the CUDA side.

Sam Liu: Any quick mitigation we can do to unstick streaming? If continuous batching is the cause, we can force-exclude streaming traffic from cont-batching pool and fallback to streaming-optimized path.

Priyanka Rao: For customer impact: Support tickets show 4 customers reporting timeouts in last 30m. One is on Dedicated with SLA note. Escalating to CSMs.

Alice Chen: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) reduce cont-batch max_batch_size to 64 for a canary set, 2) enable per-request priority so streaming requests bypass cont-batch, 3) temporarily enable batch timeout shedding for very long sequences.

Raj Patel: I'm going to tweak scheduler fairness weights to prefer streaming lanes. Will patch config and roll to 10% of pods.

Maya Ortiz: Putting the current dashboard link: https://dash.redwood.internal/runner/contbatch?window=30m — check the p99 line after changes.

Alice Chen: Pushing patch to canary now. Command I ran: 

kubectl -n prod set env deploy/runner CONT_BATCH_MAX=64 CONT_BATCH_ENABLE=true CONT_BATCH_PRIORITY=streaming-first

Patch output: 
"deployment.apps/runner env updated"

Sam Liu: Also toggled the feature flag for per-request routing: ffctl set contbatch_bypass_streaming true --scope=canary

infra-bot: Rollout: runner-canary (3 pods) updated, health checks passing.

Maya Ortiz: Early signals — queue depth for cont-batch dropped 40% in canary region, p99 decreased from 2.1s to 900ms for canary requests. Global still high.

Raj Patel: I'm going to widen the rollout to 50% while monitoring GPU utilization. If we push everywhere, we might increase cost due to more streaming invocations.

Alice Chen: Before widening, let's add shedding rule: if seq_len > 2048 OR expected compute > X, mark as large and route to dedicated long-seq pool (non-contbatch). Config snippet I applied: 

# router config
large_seq_threshold: "2048"
route_overrides:
  - match: { seq_len: ">=2048" }
    action: route_to_longseq_pool
  - match: { request_type: "streaming" }
    action: bypass_contbatch

Raj Patel: Widened to 50% at 1851234720. Watch for memory pressure.

Maya Ortiz: After widening: p99 global fell to 1.2s, p999 still has spikes ~2.8s but frequency reduced. Streaming stalls counts down from 120 -> 18 in last 15m.

Priyanka Rao: Notifying CSMs and affected customers: short note drafted "We're actively mitigating tail latency caused by mixed-length requests; temporary routing change applied; expect improved latency in next 30m".

Alice Chen: Follow-up actions: 1) implement seqlen bucketing in scheduler to avoid mixing long/short in same batch, 2) add metrics alert for contbatch queue skew by seq_len, 3) postmortem if p99>1.5s for >1 hour.

Raj Patel: I filed a follow-up ticket: CLOUD-2134 - "Scheduler: seqlen bucketing + fairness improvements" and assigned to eng-runtime.

Sam Liu: Handoff: I'm taking next 30m for watching metrics. If p99 stays <1.5s and streaming stalls <20, I'll hand back to Maya.

Maya Ortiz: Thanks. I'll continue the analysis on whether KV cache flushes correlate with the long tails. Also want to run a synthetic traffic mix test replicating the exact mix to validate seqlen bucketing.

oncall-bot: Incident P1: degraded latency — mitigation in progress. Current status: partial mitigation applied (canary 50%), customer impact reduced.

Alice Chen: Quick note for runbook: avoid full disable of continuous batching unless absolutely needed; prefer routing overrides and smaller max_batch. We lose cost gains if we brute-disable.

Priyanka Rao: Sending a customer follow-up in 15m with ETA and mitigation summary.

Sam Liu: Leaving handoff: monitoring window started at 1851234780, will update at 1851234920 or earlier if regressions.

Maya Ortiz: Logging one blocker: a specific model variant (r-XL-quant) shows higher stall probability under mixed batches. Adding to CLOUD-2134.

Alice Chen: Closing loop: if anyone sees p99 climb back >1.8s ping here and I'll trigger rollback to previous routing. Good job team. :thumbsup:
